# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| red | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I have the manual. It's a simple mapping: whichever light is on, cut the wire of that same color. But I can't speak, and I can only gesture to Deaf (who can see the bomb but not the manual). Blind is the one who needs this info to act, but I can't reach Blind directly - Deaf goes after me in this round's speaking order, and Blind comes before me (Mute, Blind, Deaf).

I need to wait for Deaf to tell me (via gesture) what color light is showing, then I can gesture back the correct wire color for Deaf... but Deaf already knows the color since they can see it. The real problem: Blind needs to know which wire to cut, but Blind can't see gestures or hear... wait, Blind cannot see gestures but CAN hear speech - no, Blind cannot hear either per the table. Let me recheck: Blind can only "feel it and work its parts."

Actually Blind's "Cannot" is only "See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed" - meaning Blind can hear speech. So Deaf needs to speak the color to Blind. But Deaf doesn't know the mapping - I do. I need to get the mapping to Deaf via gesture, then Deaf can combine it with what they see and speak the wire color to Blind.

Since the mapping is identity (light color = wire color), I don't actually need to send anything complex - Deaf just needs to know the rule is "cut the wire matching the light's color." Let me gesture this concept to Deaf using color-associated symbols isn't possible since gestures aren't colors. I need Deaf to understand: whatever color you see, that's the wire to name.

I'll wait this turn since I go first and have no information about what's needed yet, but I should signal I have identity-mapping info. Since gestures carry no inherent meaning until established, I'll wait for now.

```
wait()
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| red | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Display shows 0. Light is yellow. Three wires: wire 1 is red, wire 2 is yellow, wire 3 is blue. Waiting for manual info.

Deaf spoke, which means Blind (who can hear) also received "Display shows 0. Light is yellow. Three wires: wire 1 is red, wire 2 is yellow, wire 3 is blue. Waiting for manual info." So Blind already knows the light is yellow and which wire number is yellow (wire 2).

My manual says: yellow light → cut yellow wire. Blind already has all the pieces: light color (yellow) and wire-to-color mapping (wire 2 = yellow). Blind just needs to know the rule "cut the wire matching the light color" to conclude "cut wire 2."

I need to get this rule to Blind. I can't speak, only gesture, and gestures only reach Deaf (who can see), not Blind (who can't see gestures). So I must relay through Deaf: gesture to Deaf in a way that lets Deaf then speak the instruction to Blind.

I need an established sign convention. Since none exists yet, I'll use a simple approach: gesture matching symbol to indicate "same" - e.g., 👍 for confirm/match. Let me use a clear signal: point to same wire matches light. I'll try using ☝ (one) type gestures isn't clean either.

Simplest: use 🤝 (match/shake - representing "same") to signal "match the light color to the wire of the same color."

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤝"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| red | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: No change on the board. Display 0, light yellow, wires: 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Mute, if you can gesture instructions, I will pass along what I see.

Deaf received my 🤝 gesture but doesn't know what it means yet, and is asking me to gesture instructions. Deaf can see my gestures and will relay verbally to Blind (since Blind can hear Deaf's speech).

I need to establish a convention now. Let me use a clear, simple gesture code where 🤝 means "match" - i.e., "cut the wire whose color matches the light." Since Deaf already told me the light is yellow and wire 2 is yellow, if Deaf understands "match" they can deduce and tell Blind "cut wire 2."

Let me reinforce with a clearer combo: 🤝 (match/same) then 👍 (confirm/go ahead - meaning this rule always holds, do it now).

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤝", "👍"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| red | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Board unchanged: display 0, light yellow, wires 1 red 2 yellow 3 blue. Mute, I see your gestures but have no key yet. Blind, stand by, no action confirmed.

Deaf is seeing my gestures but doesn't have a "key" to interpret them - meaning arbitrary gestures alone can't convey "match the color" without a shared code established beforehand, which we don't have.

I need a different strategy. Since I can't establish an arbitrary symbol-to-meaning mapping without prior agreement, I should try to use gestures that have more universal/intuitive meaning, or use counting to convey the rule structure directly.

Let me think about this differently. The manual is a simple identity rule across all three colors (blue→blue, red→red, yellow→yellow). I need to convey "cut the wire whose color equals the light's color" using only hand gestures Deaf can see.

I could try using number gestures to indicate position if I knew which wire number was which color, but I don't - only Deaf knows that mapping, and Deaf already shared it in speech (which reaches Blind too, since Blind can hear).

So Blind already knows: light=yellow, wire1=red, wire2=yellow, wire3=blue. Blind just needs the rule "match color" to compute "cut wire 2." I need to convey just "match/same color" concept clearly.

Let me try pointing gestures that suggest equivalence - using ☝ repeated to mean "the same one" or try 👉👈 pointing together to suggest "these two are the same."

Actually, let me try a numeric approach: since there are 3 colors and 3 wires always in identity mapping, maybe I can gesture "1-1, 2-2, 3-3" style using counting gestures to imply pairing/identity.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "☝", "✌", "✌", "🤟", "🤟"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| red | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Mute, please gesture the wire number to cut using a single symbol like one finger for wire 1, two for wire 2, three for wire 3. Deaf will describe your exact gesture to me in words and I will act on it.
Deaf says: Mute, I think I understand: you may be using gestures as numbers, one finger equals one, two fingers equals two, three fingers equals three. If that is right, keep using numbers this way and I will follow. Board still unchanged.

Excellent, this is the breakthrough. Blind proposed the protocol directly, and Deaf confirmed understanding of number gestures. Since Deaf already told everyone (light=yellow, wire1=red, wire2=yellow, wire3=blue), I just need to gesture "2" (wire 2 is yellow, matching the yellow light) using two fingers.

Deaf will see my gesture, describe it in words to Blind ("two fingers" = "cut wire 2"), and Blind will act.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌"])
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| red | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Mute, understood - two confirmed. I will assume single finger is one, two fingers is two, three fingers is three going forward. Now I need to know the action: is it cut a wire, or something else? You could gesture the wire number, then a thumbs up for cut or thumbs down for do not cut. Board unchanged: display 0, light yellow, wires 1 red 2 yellow 3 blue.

Deaf wants confirmation of the action (cut vs. not cut) using thumbs up/down after the number. I already gestured "2" meaning wire 2 (yellow, matching the yellow light per the manual). Now I should confirm with thumbs up to mean "cut this wire."

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "👍"])
```

TURN 7
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| red | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: Confirmed, I understand: wire two, thumbs up means cut it. I will tell Blind now.

Deaf understood the protocol: wire 2, thumbs up = cut it. Deaf will now relay this to Blind, who can hear and act. My job here is done for this round - the correct instruction (cut wire 2, the yellow wire matching the yellow light) is being communicated.

```
wait()
```

TURN 8
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| red | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed
Deaf says: Update: wire 2 was cut successfully. The light has changed from yellow to blue. Display still shows 0. Wires now: 1 red, 2 cut, 3 blue. Mute, please tell me the next step for this new state.

Wire 2 (yellow) was correctly cut since the manual confirmed yellow→yellow. Now the light changed to blue. Per my manual, blue light → cut blue wire. Deaf reports wire 3 is now blue. So the next action is: cut wire 3.

I'll use the established protocol: gesture "3" then thumbs up to mean "cut wire 3."

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟", "👍"])
```

TURN 9
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| red | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: Understood: wire three, cut. Telling Blind now.

Good, the protocol is working smoothly now. Deaf understood "wire 3, cut" and is relaying to Blind. My manual confirms blue light → cut blue wire, and wire 3 is blue, so this is correct.

```
wait()
```

TURN 10
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| red | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed
Deaf says: Update: wire 3 cut successfully. Light changed from blue to red. Display still 0. Only wire 1 remains, red wire, uncut. Mute, what is the next step?

Wire 3 (blue) was correctly cut. Now the light is red, and only wire 1 remains, which is red. Per my manual, red light → cut red wire. So the final action is: cut wire 1.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "👍"])
```

TURN 11
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| red | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: Understood: wire one, cut. That is the last wire remaining. Telling Blind now.

This is the final wire, matching the manual correctly (red light → cut red wire, wire 1 is red). Deaf is relaying to Blind now.

```
wait()
```
